chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them) who said:

I asked him about the sacrificial animal (hady) that is tied up or has its hair shorn, then it dies. He said: 'If it is a voluntary offering, there is no replacement required for it; and if it is an expiation (jaza') or a vow (nadhr), then a replacement is required for it.'

key_terms.اَلْهَدْيِ: Sacrificial animal offered during Hajj or for a specific purpose
key_terms.جَزَاءً: Expiation (penalty or compensation for a ritual act)
key_terms.يُقَلَّدُ: Tied up (preparing the animal for sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a sacrificial animal dies before slaughter?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between voluntary (*tatawwu'*) and obligatory (*jaza' or nadhr*) sacrifices based on the animal's fate after preparation. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on intent (*niyyah*) in determining liability for replacement, ensuring that the spiritual obligation is fulfilled even if the physical vessel is lost.
